text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure, or hypertension, is diagnosed when readings are consistently at or above 130/80 mm Hg.
Blood pressure is recorded as two numbers. The top number is systolic pressure (when the heart beats), and the bottom number is diastolic pressure (when the heart rests between beats).

list.snippet: Normal: Less than 120 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic.
Elevated: 120–129 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic.
Stage 1 Hypertension: 130–139 mm Hg systolic or 80–89 mm Hg diastolic.
Stage 2 Hypertension: 140 mm Hg or higher systolic or 90 mm Hg or higher diastolic.

Hypertensive Crisis: Higher than 180 mm Hg systolic and/or higher than 120 mm Hg diastolic. Readings this high require immediate medical attention, especially if there are symptoms like chest pain or shortness of breath.

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more details about these definitions through the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention or the American Heart Association.
